items.title: KTRE: Polk County district judge publicly admonished over COVID-19 vaccine/visitation order and plea-certification rule
items.summary: East Texas broadcast coverage dated Sept. 16, 2026 reports the State Commission on Judicial Conduct publicly admonished 258th District Judge Travis E. Kitchens Jr. (Polk, San Jacinto, and Trinity Counties) after its Aug. 12-13, 2026 meeting. The Commission found two failures to comply with and maintain competence in the law: requiring defendants and counsel to certify review of court-mandated prison/parole materials before the court would accept a plea, and ordering parents in a contested family case to obtain a COVID-19 vaccine or a negative test within 72 hours of visitation. The official sanction date on the FY2026 roster is Aug. 25, 2026 (CJC No. 21-1342). This is additional local recirculation of an already-logged official action, not a new Commission vote.
items.quality: Local network affiliate quoting the official public-admonition language. High reliability for the fact of the sanction; the primary source remains the SCJC FY2026 public-sanctions list and the signed order.

items.title: Hays Free Press series: mothers allege Hays County family court (Judge Karl Hays) failed children in abuse-related cases
items.summary: Local reporting updated into mid-September 2026 presents accounts from multiple mothers who say Hays County family-law Associate Judge Karl Hays discounted abuse evidence, limited forensic interviews as hearsay, and issued orders they contend were contrary to the children's best interest. One mother stated she was fined $500 for a false report even after CPS found reason to believe and a related indictment issued. These are litigant allegations published by a local paper; they are not State Commission on Judicial Conduct findings.
items.quality: Local weekly reporting of named litigant accounts. Medium reliability for the fact that families are publicly alleging patterns; low reliability as proof of judicial misconduct until docket records or an SCJC action confirm specifics.

items.title: Former legislator Lon Burnam files petition seeking removal of Tarrant County Judge Tim O'Hare for official misconduct
items.summary: On Sept. 9, 2026, former Texas House member Lon Burnam filed a petition seeking Tarrant County Judge Tim O'Hare's removal from office, alleging official misconduct under the Local Government Code for using official authority to have Burnam removed from the Aug. 4 Commissioners Court meeting and issuing a 180-day criminal-trespass warning. Burnam was arrested at that meeting; the petition is a civil removal action, not an SCJC sanction. Related First Amendment suits against the county remain pending.
items.quality: Nonprofit local newsroom citing a filed petition and contemporaneous meeting coverage. High reliability that the petition was filed; merits and legal sufficiency unresolved.

items.title: Texas Supreme Court Advisory Committee revisits third-party litigation-finance disclosure after prior no recommendation
items.summary: On Sept. 10, 2026, the Supreme Court Advisory Committee discussed draft approaches to disclosing outside litigation finance after recommending against a rule in August 2025. Options under discussion include in-camera review of funder identities and a good-cause standard before disclosure. The Texas Business Court already requires funder disclosure to flag conflicts. This is institutional rule-making, not a misconduct finding.
items.quality: National legal-trade reporting of an on-the-record advisory committee session. High reliability on the fact of the discussion; no rule has been adopted.

items.title: Secondary coverage of Aug. 25 SCJC public admonition of Judge Travis E. Kitchens Jr. (vaccine/visitation and plea-certification rules)
items.summary: Texas Scorecard on Sept. 10 summarized the State Commission on Judicial Conduct's Aug. 25, 2026 public admonition of 258th District Judge Travis E. Kitchens Jr. (Polk, San Jacinto, Trinity Counties). The Commission found he required parents to be vaccinated or produce a negative COVID-19 test before visitation and separately required defendants and counsel to review specified materials before the court would accept a plea. The Commission characterized the conduct as a failure to comply with and maintain competence in the law. This item is recirculation of an already-logged official sanction.
items.quality: Advocacy outlet summarizing an official SCJC order already on the FY2026 public-sanctions list. Use the official roster as the primary source for the fact of the sanction.

items.title: Midland County appoints Judge-elect Jay Marquez as acting county judge after Terry Johnson suspension
items.summary: Midland County Commissioners Court voted Sept. 2 to appoint County Judge-elect Jay Marquez as acting county judge under Government Code section 26.017 following the SCJC's Aug. 26 suspension with pay of incumbent Terry Johnson. Marquez, who defeated Johnson in the primary and is scheduled to take office Jan. 1, 2027, was sworn in the same day. The appointment ensures continuity while criminal charges and a Chapter 87 removal action remain pending.
items.quality: Local newspaper of record + contemporaneous broadcast report; high reliability on the appointment action.

items.title: SCJC issues three public sanctions (Aug. 25 batch): Barry Green, Francisco Frank Gutierrez, Travis E. Kitchens Jr.
items.source: State Commission on Judicial Conduct (public sanctions list)
items.summary: On Aug. 25, 2026 the Commission publicly admonished Hon. Barry Green (Municipal Court, Decatur, Wise County, CJC 25-0046) and Hon. Travis E. Kitchens, Jr. (258th District Court, Livingston, Polk County, CJC 21-1342). It issued a public reprimand and order of additional education to Hon. Francisco Frank Gutierrez (Justice of the Peace Pct. 3 Pl. 1, Lubbock County, CJC 25-0078). Full underlying orders were not immediately detailed in secondary coverage; the official list confirms the actions and case numbers.
items.quality: Official SCJC public-sanctions roster. Highest reliability for the fact and date of the sanctions; detailed findings require the individual orders.

items.title: Free speech lawsuits against Tarrant County Judge Tim O'Hare awaiting Fifth Circuit decision
items.summary: Two federal lawsuits allege Tarrant County and County Judge Tim O'Hare violated the First Amendment by removing speakers from Commissioners Court meetings under county decorum rules. A related case is before the U.S. Fifth Circuit; U.S. District Judge Mark Pittman paused the newer Kirkland suit pending that ruling. Coverage also notes a recent meeting in which the courtroom was cleared after applause and a former state lawmaker was arrested after continuing to speak. This is civil constitutional litigation, not an SCJC sanction.
items.quality: Local nonprofit newsroom citing docket activity; high reliability on procedural posture, merits unresolved.

items.title: Midland County commissioners set Sept. 2 meeting to appoint acting county judge after SCJC suspension
items.summary: After the State Commission on Judicial Conduct suspended County Judge Terry Johnson with pay on Aug. 26, Midland County Commissioners Court scheduled a Sept. 2 special meeting to appoint an acting county judge under Government Code section 26.017. Johnson was indicted Aug. 19 on two third-degree felonies and a misdemeanor tied to posting a document containing personal identifying information. A separate Chapter 87 removal suit by the district attorney remains pending.
items.quality: Local newspaper of record plus official meeting notice.

items.title: SCJC Order of Suspension: Hon. Terry Johnson, Midland County Judge (with pay)
items.summary: Interim Chair Hon. Ken Wise signed an Order of Suspension on Aug. 26, 2026. The Commission recites the Aug. 19 indictment in Cause No. DCR-26-00807 and suspends Johnson with pay until the charges are dismissed, he is acquitted, or the Commission orders otherwise. The Commission reserved authority to reconsider if additional information arrives.
items.quality: Official signed SCJC order. Highest reliability for the fact of suspension.

items.title: Judges in malpractice case received $32,500 in contributions from Baker Botts and counsel
items.summary: Reporting on campaign-finance records found Baker Botts and related counsel contributed at least $32,500 to five judges connected to a Houston malpractice/arbitration matter, including $6,500 to Justice Ken Wise of the 14th Court of Appeals while the appeal was pending. The article states the contributions do not by themselves establish wrongdoing and do not show the contributions affected any ruling. Questions raised concern disclosure, recusal, and appearance of impartiality.
items.quality: Legal trade reporting citing contribution records. Reliable on dollar amounts and timing; no finding of misconduct.

items.title: Maverick County Judge Ramsey English Cantu resigns after Chapter 87 suspension
items.source: San Antonio Express-News / Laredo Morning Times
items.summary: Former Maverick County Judge Ramsey English Cantu resigned after months under a court-ordered suspension in a Chapter 87 petition alleging official misconduct and incompetency. A court had also restricted his social-media speech. He stated he was not leaving under indictment. Specific underlying facts of the civil allegations were limited in public coverage.
items.quality: Hearst local reporting. Reliable on resignation and prior suspension.

items.title: Judge John Roach Jr. recused from next steps of Karmelo Anthony case
items.summary: Visiting Judge Sid Harle recused Collin County District Judge John Roach Jr. from remaining proceedings in the Karmelo Anthony case. Defense argued Roach's public comments about the verdict and his decision to close an overflow room created an appearance of bias and a public-trial issue. Harle said he personally believed Roach could be fair but found the defense showing sufficient for recusal.
items.quality: Metro newspaper of record covering an on-the-record recusal hearing.
